title: Draft 2-3 test prompts in evals/evals.json
description: Create evals/evals.json under the skill directory with 2-3 realistic prompts. Examples: 'I'm in diy mode — add a created_at timestamp to the users table and surface it on the profile page'; 'guide me through adding a debounced search input to the dashboard'; 'diy mode: refactor the auth middleware to support service tokens'. Each should exercise: read-the-code, produce-the-to-do, gitignore-DIY_TODO.md, refuse-to-code-on-followup.

title: Document escape hatch and exit behavior
description: If user says 'just write it', 'do it for me', etc. while in diy-mode: HARD REFUSE, remind them this is muscle-building mode, tell them they must say '/exit-diy' (or 'diy off', 'stop diy') first. Mode persists across turns. Only the explicit exit phrase ends it. After exit, the agent returns to normal behavior on the next turn.

title: Document follow-up behavior: review, hint, never write
description: When user comes back with 'done with #3' or 'stuck on #5': agent reviews user's code (read-only), points at issues, gives PROSE-ONLY hints (concepts, patterns, what to read, shape of the answer — no code, no type signatures, no pseudo-code, no snippets). Updates the checkbox in DIY_TODO.md when user confirms done. Pulls next item.

title: Document Beads-as-canonical-source behavior
description: When Beads tasks exist for the current work, the DIY_TODO.md is rendered FROM the Beads tasks (one checkbox per child task, preserving order). When no Beads tasks exist, agent produces the to-do directly. The Beads tree remains the durable record; DIY_TODO.md is the working surface.

title: Document DIY_TODO.md format and append behavior
description: Spec: file at ./DIY_TODO.md in repo root. On each invocation, APPEND a new section with timestamped header (### YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM - <one-line task summary>). Each item is a checkbox bullet, one per file-or-function change. Format: '- [ ] <imperative verb> <what> in <file>: <one-line constraint or why>'. No code blocks, no type signatures, no snippets. Also: agent must add DIY_TODO.md to .gitignore if not already there (one-time, asks first).

title: Document the gate: what's blocked vs allowed
description: Section explaining: BLOCKED = Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit on source, git commit/push, migrations, mutating scripts. ALLOWED = Read, Grep, run tests/lints/typecheck, git status/log/diff, fetch URLs, grill-me, Beads writes, and writing DIY_TODO.md (the skill's own output artifact). Explain the why: user's engineering muscles atrophy when agent does the work.

title: Scaffold diy-mode skill directory and SKILL.md frontmatter
description: Create /Users/kevinkabeya/.claude/skills/diy-mode/SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name=diy-mode, pushy description that triggers on /diy, 'diy mode', 'guide me', 'don't write the code', 'just tell me what to do', 'practice mode', etc). Include the top-level overview: this skill is a gate at the execution boundary.

title: Build diy-mode skill: agent produces to-do markdown instead of executing work
description:
Skill that gates the agent at the execution boundary. Normal reasoning/planning/Beads flow is unchanged — the agent simply refuses to write code or mutate the repo, and instead produces a markdown checklist for the human to follow. Purpose: keep the user's programming muscles strong.

Resolved decisions from grill-me:

Q: How should diy-mode get activated?
A: Explicit trigger only (/diy, "diy mode", "guide me"). No auto-detection.

Q: Investigation scope before producing the to-do?
A: Full normal flow — diy-mode only gates the execution step. Agent reads code, greps, can use grill-me, can write Beads tasks, etc.

Q: What stays allowed vs gated?
A: Blocks ALL writes/edits to source — Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, mutating git ops, migrations, scripts that touch the codebase. Read-only ops still allowed: read, grep, run tests/lints/typecheck, git status/log, fetch URLs.

Q: Granularity of each to-do item?
A: One bullet per file-or-function change. E.g. "add created_at column to users table in db/schema.ts", not "implement auth" and not "rename folder".

Q: Relationship to Beads?
A: Markdown is the execution view of Beads. Beads remains canonical; markdown is rendered from the Beads tasks at execution time.

Q: What does the agent do when the user comes back after working on items?
A: Stays in diy-mode. Reviews user's code, points at issues, gives hints, pulls the next item. Never writes the fix.

Q: How much can the agent help when user is stuck?
A: Prose hints only — no code, no type signatures, no snippets, no pseudo-code. Concepts, patterns, what to read, shape of the answer.

Q: What if user explicitly asks the agent to write code?
A: Hard refuse. User must exit diy-mode first. Pairs with explicit-exit-only rule.

Q: How does diy-mode end?
A: Explicit exit phrase only ("/exit-diy", "diy off", "stop diy"). Persists across turns until then.

Q: Where does the markdown to-do live?
A: ./DIY_TODO.md in repo root. Single rolling file with timestamped section headers appended on each invocation. Gitignored.

Q: Where should this plan be tracked?
A: Beads epic + child tasks, then write the skill.
